newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian courts sentence 15 Islamists to death.
newsitem.headline: Algerian courts sentence 15 Islamists to death.

text.p: Two Algerian courts have sentenced 15 Moslem fundamentalists to death for "belonging to armed terrorist groups" the official Algerian news agency APS said on Wednesday.
Nine, condemned by the criminal court in Tizi-Ouzou in northeastern Algeria, were also charged with "premeditated murder and ambushes, and financing a terrorist group".

It was not immediately clear whether the nine, sentenced on Monday, were in court or were tried in their absence. APS said the same court also sentenced to death three other men who were still on the run.

In Medea town, the criminal court sentenced three Moslem fundamentalists to death on Tuesday. They were tried in their absence on charges of "belonging to an armed terrorist group aiming to spread death".
Three others facing the same charges were acquitted, the agency said, without detailing whether they were in court for the trial.
Medea, 60 km (40 miles) southwest of Algiers, has been a focal point of trials in the five-year-old conflict between security forces and Moslem guerrillas.
Last Monday, the court there sentenced six men to death in their absence for belonging to "armed terrorist groups, pre-meditated murder, ambushes, and arson".
On December 1, APS reported that the same court had condemned to death 23 members of a "terrorist" group -- all on the run.
APS on Tuesday said a criminal court in Tlemcen, 440-km (275-miles), west of Algiers, convicted 12 men, also on the run, to death for involvement in guerrilla activities.
More than 1,200 Moslem fundamentalists have been condemned to death, mostly in absentia, since 1993 when Algerian courts started trials of activists.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
